title: Tor amplitude in a fixed interval is local on open neighbourhoods
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with chosen derived localizations for module sheaves on $X$ and on each open subscheme [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $a\leq b$ be integers. Suppose every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ such that for every $\mathcal O_U$-module $G$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$, $H^i(L(U\hookrightarrow X)^*E\otimes^L G)=0$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. Then for every $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$, $H^i(E\otimes^L G)=0$. The interval is fixed before choosing the neighbourhood or test module; no compactness or quasi-coherence is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08CG (definition-tor-amplitude); Tag 09U9 (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), proof and finite-subcover consequence

proof.text: Use essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q and [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to obtain a K-flat model of every derived object. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-derived-tensor-comparison] to constant functors on Discrete PUnit and apply homologyFunctorFactors. This proves tensor_vanishes_iff: the existential model vanishing predicate [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes] is equivalent to zero homology of E tensor the degree-zero single of G. Both implications are proved, and the reverse implication explicitly supplies the model.

For an open immersion f, extract the defining K-flat counit of the chosen [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Termwise tensorPullback f and restrictFunctor f are isomorphic by uniqueness of left adjoints to the same pushforward [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. On a K-flat model the counit is invertible; combine it with the quotient comparison and the termwise adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism. For an arbitrary E, transport along its K-flat model and mapDerivedCategoryFactors, using overFunctorEquiv. This constructs open_pullback_restriction_iso in the actual chosen localization universe. For homology use the already proved source-library Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso, in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.ExactFunctor.

Fix G and i outside the interval, and choose U(x) from the hypothesis. Apply the local hypothesis to the exact restriction of G. By tensor_vanishes_iff its local derived tensor homology is zero. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-open-restriction-universes], open_pullback_restriction_iso and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor to identify this with the homology of the restriction of E tensor G[0]. Transport through Functor.mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso and overFunctorEquiv. Thus the global homology sheaf restricts to zero on every U(x).

The chosen opens cover X, since x belongs to U(x); in Lean their indexed supremum is top. Apply the already proved library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isZero_of_iSup_eq_top in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Sheaf to the global homology sheaf and the local zero restrictions. This is the open-cover version of the sheaf separatedness argument in Tag 09U9. Finally use the reverse implication of tensor_vanishes_iff. The empty-scheme case is included by the same supremum and local vanishing theorem.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09U9 (lemma-tor-amplitude-stalk), exact restriction and local detection of zero; the existing proved open-cover criterion replaces the final stalk criterion.

lean.statement:
theorem torAmplitude_of_open_neighbourhoods (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (h : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
      ∀ (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)) (i : ℤ),
        i < a ∨ b < i → schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes U.toScheme
          ((derivedPullback U.ι).obj E) G i) :
    ∀ (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) (i : ℤ),
      i < a ∨ b < i → schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes X E G i
